To compute \( P^2 \), we need to multiply the transition matrix \( P \) by itself:

\[
P = \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & 0.5 \\ 0.2 & 0.8 \end{bmatrix}
\]

Calculating \( P^2 \):

\[
P^2 = P \cdot P = \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & 0.5 \\ 0.2 & 0.8 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & 0.5 \\ 0.2 & 0.8 \end{bmatrix}
\]

We calculate the elements of the resulting matrix:

1. First row, first column:
\[
0.5 \cdot 0.5 + 0.5 \cdot 0.2 = 0.25 + 0.1 = 0.35
\]

2. First row, second column:
\[
0.5 \cdot 0.5 + 0.5 \cdot 0.8 = 0.25 + 0.4 = 0.65
\]

3. Second row, first column:
\[
0.2 \cdot 0.5 + 0.8 \cdot 0.2 = 0.1 + 0.16 = 0.26
\]

4. Second row, second column:
\[
0.2 \cdot 0.5 + 0.8 \cdot 0.8 = 0.1 + 0.64 = 0.74
\]

Putting these results together, we find:

\[
P^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 0.35 & 0.65 \\ 0.26 & 0.74 \end{bmatrix}
\]

Final answer: \(\begin{bmatrix} 0.35 & 0.65 \\ 0.26 & 0.74 \end{bmatrix}\)
